cf.title: Fix exclude generated columns in COPY TO with RLS

input.subject: Fix exclude generated columns in COPY TO with RLS

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the design. The patch makes COPY TO under RLS follow the documented rule and the non-RLS path. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, asks which branches the fix is for, because a back-patch would change the output columns in a minor release. That is a fixable point for a committer to decide, and it does not stop review of the idea.

brief.title: Exclude generated columns from COPY TO when row-level security is active
brief.problem: COPY TO without a column list exports generated columns when RLS applies to the user, which contradicts the COPY documentation. The output then cannot be loaded back with COPY FROM, which rejects generated columns. Under RLS, a user with SELECT only on the non-generated columns also gets "permission denied for table".
brief.proposed_design: Under RLS, DoCopy() rewrites COPY TO into an internal SELECT that used an A_Star target list, so all non-dropped columns were included. The patch builds that target list from the attnums that CopyGetAttnums() already computes, so the RLS path copies the same columns as the non-RLS path.
user_visible_surface: COPY TO without a column list on a table with RLS active no longer outputs generated columns.
COPY TO under RLS no longer fails with "permission denied" when the user lacks SELECT only on generated columns.
author_claims: The current output violates the documented rule that generated columns are not copied without a column list.
The fix restores COPY TO / COPY FROM round-tripping under RLS.
Users who want generated columns in the output can use COPY (SELECT * FROM t) TO.
The patch makes RLS behavior match non-RLS behavior.
brief.thread_state: Jim Jones tested v1, confirmed the fix, and asked for a regression test for the column-privilege case, which v2 says it adds. Jim's question whether COPY TO should ever include generated columns got only the round-trip answer from the author.
unclear: The material does not say whether the fix is meant for back-branches, which would change output that some users may rely on.
The material does not say whether RLS policies that reference generated columns still work when the target list omits them.
The material does not say how virtual generated columns, if present, are handled.
The material does not mention partitioned tables, inheritance or views on this RLS path.

objections.title: Backpatch would change COPY TO output columns in a minor release
objections.failure_scenario: An export job runs COPY t TO under an RLS-restricted role and its consumer expects the generated column in a fixed column position. After a minor update the column disappears and every later field shifts by one. The consumer then loads wrong values or rejects the rows, and the error shows up downstream long after the upgrade.
objections.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, and its target version is None. The proposal does not say whether the fix goes to back branches or only to master. Since generated columns arrived, the RLS path has emitted them, so some exports may depend on today's column layout. Matching the documentation is a good reason to change master, but changing output shape in a minor release is a separate decision that the thread has not discussed.
objections.author_must_show: Is this fix meant for master only, and if it is meant for back branches, how would users who rely on the current RLS output learn about the change?

critic.reasoning: The entry is tagged Bugfix with target version None, and no message says which branches the fix is for. The export scenario is concrete, and the thread has not weighed a minor-release change of output columns.

refuted.title: Back-patching would silently shift COPY TO output columns under RLS
refuted.failure_scenario: A nightly job runs COPY TO as an RLS-subject role and parses fields by position, expecting the generated column. After a minor-release update the column disappears, so later fields shift by one. The job may load wrong values into the target table, and nobody sees an error.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, which suggests a back-patch, but message #1 and the commit message do not say which branches the fix is for. On released branches the current output is long-standing behavior, and some users may depend on it even though the documentation says otherwise. A committer would likely ask whether this goes to master only, with a release note.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the fix meant for master only, and if not, why is changing COPY TO output in a minor release acceptable?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which states the same back-patch question and the same shifted-column scenario.

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the COPY code and the RLS rewrite in DoCopy() would have to own it. The visible thread has the author and one reviewer.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a change in COPY TO output columns under RLS and for the back-branch decision. The code change is small and removes a difference between the RLS and non-RLS paths.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 with the requested regression test one day after the review in message #2.

priority.reason: The bug affects only COPY TO without a column list on a table with RLS and a generated column. The patch is about 6 KiB in copy.c plus rowsecurity tests, and it reuses the CopyGetAttnums() list.

precedents_retrieved.title: COPY WHERE clause generated/system column reference
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches make COPY FROM ... WHERE work with generated columns: they expand virtual generated columns in the WHERE clause and compute stored generated columns before the WHERE clause is checked. They also reject system columns other than tableoid in the WHERE clause.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed a smaller fix that rejects generated columns in COPY FROM WHERE with a clear error, and left tableoid for a separate thread. He then argued that support should not be added, because generated columns belong to the target table while the WHERE clause filters input data. Masahiko Sawada had shown that computing stored generated columns before the WHERE clause runs them before BEFORE INSERT triggers, so the WHERE clause changes the row the trigger sees.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This seems fundamentally wrong, because generated columns are a
property of the target table, but the COPY WHERE clause is meant to
filter the input data.

precedents_retrieved.title: DOCS for generated column replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an "Examples" subsection to the new "Generated Column Replication" documentation page. The examples are self-contained publication, subscription and table setups that users can paste into psql, and they show rules such as publication column lists overriding publish_generated_columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila judged the current text and example sufficient for a new feature and preferred to add more examples only after real user feedback. No one else replied in support, so vignesh C closed the entry for lack of interest, with the option to revisit if users ask for it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I still feel that the current text and example given on the page are
sufficient for now. This is a new feature, and I think it is better to
get some feedback from users.

precedents_retrieved.title: foreign key on virtual generated column
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows a foreign key on a virtual generated column, limited to ON UPDATE NO ACTION/RESTRICT and ON DELETE CASCADE/NO ACTION/RESTRICT. The RI check computes the generated value. ALTER COLUMN SET EXPRESSION and SET DATA TYPE then revalidate the constraint without a table rewrite.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only reviewer found the patches mostly fine and raised two performance points: the RI check computes virtual columns that are not in the key, and TryReuseForeignKey always forces revalidation when a virtual column is in the key. The visible messages contain no reply from the author before the withdrawal.

precedents_retrieved.title: generated columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Eisentraut proposed implementing SQL-standard generated columns (GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr)), with the generation expression stored in pg_attrdef like a default and MySQL/Oracle-style VIRTUAL|STORED syntax. Only the VIRTUAL (computed-on-read) variant was fully implemented; STORED, various ALTER TABLE forms and index support were deferred.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review by Jaime Casanova found multiple bugs: generated columns showed no value through a view, inheritance produced a malformed default and a server crash on insert, ALTER COLUMN TYPE on the referenced or generated column failed with internal errors, triggers saw NULL for the generated column, and the generation expression could be dropped via DROP DEFAULT. Based on these reviews, the commitfest manager marked the entry Returned with feedback, asking for an updated version to be resubmitted.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Based on this review, and the errors noted in upthread in the previous review,
I’m marking this Returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical decoding to output generated columns
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Smith (smithpb2250), Shubham Khanna (skhanna), Shlok Kyal (shlokkyal)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let pgoutput send generated column values in logical replication so consumers such as Debezium get a complete row. The work added replication of generated columns named in a publication column list, and then a publish_generated_columns publication parameter.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Most of the work was committed, so the entry closed with only follow-up items left. Peter Eisentraut asked how the feature should interact with the proposed virtual generated columns, which he did not think could reasonably be replicated, and said the option should state that it covers only stored generated columns. That point was still open a month later, so Michael Paquier returned the idle entry and suggested resubmitting once the virtual generated column question is settled.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As of now this thread is
just waiting on author and idle in the CF app for no real purpose.  I
have marked it as returned with feedback, and I'd suggest to come back
to it and resubmit once the horizon is clear (one item being related
to virtual generated columns).

precedents_retrieved.title: DOCS - Generated Column Logical Replication Examples
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an "Examples" subsection to the new "Generated Column Replication" section of the logical replication documentation. The examples are self-contained psql scripts with a publication, a subscription and tables, and they show rules such as a publication column list overriding publish_generated_columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry. The thread shows only the opening message, with no replies, so the visible messages do not show why.

precedents_retrieved.title: Infinite Autovacuum loop caused by failing virtual generated column expression
precedents_retrieved.summary: When an extended statistics expression raises an error during ANALYZE, for example a virtual generated column computing 100 / a on a row where a = 0, the patch skips that statistics object with a WARNING. ANALYZE then completes for the rest of the table, which stops autovacuum from retrying the table every minute.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed and Bharath Rupireddy saw the repeated failure as existing behaviour, present for expression statistics since PG14. With the default 1 minute retry interval it does not flood the log, a later retry may succeed, and the user can drop or fix the statistics object. Bharath Rupireddy also said a fix only for extended statistics makes behaviour inconsistent with other analyze errors. He showed that v2 catches the error without re-throwing or aborting a subtransaction, which can leave the transaction inconsistent ("transaction left non-empty SPI stack"). He then withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It's not new, it's not a flood, it may succeed on a later retry, and the user can drop or fix the offending stats object in this specific case.

precedents_retrieved.title: revamp row-security tracking
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces the per-query tracking of whether row security applies with a global queue of row-security nest levels. get_row_security_policies() marks the levels, and higher-level callers such as fireRIRrules() read them, with cleanup after an ERROR.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed objected to the global variables, the hooks into transaction management, and setting the flag far from where RLS policies are applied. He proposed adding a hasRowSecurity output parameter to fireRIRrules() instead. The author wrote that design as v2 but worried it did not go far enough, and later planned to withdraw for lack of interest. Tom Lane replied that the topic needs more thought and suggested other designs, and the visible messages show no work after that.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm also not a fan of using global variables in this way, or the
resulting need to hook into the transaction management system to tidy
up. The end result is that the places where the flag is set are moved
further away from where RLS policies are applied, which IMO makes the
code much harder to follow.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
Reverted commit(s): Ensure that RowExprs and whole-row Vars produce the expected column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit bf7ca1587, I had the bright idea that we could make the
result of a whole-row Var (that is, foo.*) track any column aliases
that had been applied to the FROM entry the Var refers to.  However,
that's not terribly logically consistent, because now the output of
the Var is no longer of the named composite type that the Var claims
to emit.  bf7ca1587 tried to handle that by changing the output
tuple values to be labeled with a blessed RECORD type, but that's
really pretty disastrous: we can wind up storing such tuples onto
disk, whereupon they're not readable by other sessions.

The only practical fix I can see is to give up on what bf7ca1587
tried to do, and say that the column names of tuples produced by
a whole-row Var are always those of the underlying named composite
type, query aliases or no.  While this introduces some inconsistencies,
it removes others, so it's not that awful in the abstract.  What *is*
kind of awful is to make such a behavioral change in a back-patched
bug fix.  But corrupt data is worse, so back-patched it will be.

(A workaround available to anyone who's unhappy about this is to
introduce an extra level of sub-SELECT, so that the whole-row Var is
referring to the sub-SELECT's output and not to a named table type.
Then the Var is of type RECORD to begin with and there's no issue.)

Per report from Miles Delahunty.  The faulty commit dates to 9.5,
so back-patch to all supported branches.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the retrieved precedents contain no earlier attempt at this idea, and the thread does not point to any earlier discussion. The patch fixes a mismatch with documented COPY behaviour, so there is no recorded rejection reason to carry over from the prior-attempts angle.
The change makes the RLS path match the documented non-RLS behavior, and the stricter column-privilege handling follows the same rule. Only the backpatch question remains from this angle.

The patch only changes the target list of the internal SELECT that DoCopy() builds for COPY TO under RLS. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column, wire protocol message or extension-facing API, so this angle has nothing to object to. Back-branch output changes are a behaviour question for other angles.

No security objection. The patch narrows what the RLS rewrite of COPY TO reads to the columns the non-RLS path already checks, so a column-privileged user gets only the columns they are granted, as in message #2. Two points depend on code not shown: that policy quals on generated columns still apply, and that virtual generated columns are excluded.

From the maintenance angle the design is small and lowers long-run cost, because the RLS path now uses the same CopyGetAttnums() list as the non-RLS path, so the two paths cannot drift apart. It adds no hot-path cost, no API and no new dependency.

This is a bug fix that makes COPY TO under RLS follow the documented rule and the non-RLS path, so no existing feature or extension gives the same result. An explicit column list is a workaround for affected users, but it does not fix the documented default, and the fix adds no new mechanism.

This is a bug fix: COPY TO under RLS breaks the documented rule on generated columns and the COPY TO / COPY FROM round trip, and it raises a false permission error under column privileges. Any RLS user who runs COPY TO on a table with a generated column meets it, so demand needs no separate evidence. Whether the fix goes to back branches is a design question for another angle.
